facts.text: Banks, Idaho, takes its name from Merle Banks, a rancher who filed a homestead claim in 1908 along the Payette River.
Banks sits where the North and South Forks of the Payette River merge, forming the main stem of the Payette.
The Idaho Northern Railroad ran through Banks from 1911 to 1913, hauling timber from Long Valley and livestock to Emmett.
In 1997, a massive landslide buried Lower Banks under mud and rocks, but timely evacuations saved every resident.
Banks is the main put‑in for the Payette River’s Class II‑III rapids, drawing rafters, kayakers, and tube‑riders from June to September.
Banks experiences hot, humid summers and severely cold winters, with July highs around 90°F and January lows near 20°F.
